messages:
Maya: Heads-up — seeing repeated flapping on gpu-pool-usw1 for the last ~4h. Pattern: external QPS spike -> HPA scales pods -> Cluster Autoscaler spins up nodes -> VPA recommendation/eviction -> pods bounce -> CA sees lower utilization and tries to scale down. Latency blips reported by prod-api. Anyone else? :eyes:
Sam: Yup, got the same alerts. Prometheus shows short 30–90s QPS bursts up to ~800, baseline ~150. CA logs show scale-up then scale-down within ~6m. Drains take ~2m and cause pod reschedules which trigger HPA again.
Jia: Are we running VPA in auto-evict mode on model-serving? If VPA performs eviction during node churn that will amplify the loop.
Maya: Checking — VPA objects in model-serving are set to mode: Auto for a few deployments. That might be the kicker.
Leo: Quick facts: HPA target is external QPS 200, min pods 2, max 40. No explicit behavior configured. CA settings: balance-similar-node-groups=true, scale-down-delay=10m (default). Nodepool gpu-pool-usw1 min=0,max=12.
Sam: Short list of mitigations I want to try:
  1) Add HPA behavior to stabilize scaleDown (stabilizationWindowSeconds >= 300) and cap growth policy to avoid instant huge scale-ups.
  2) Smooth external metric via a Prometheus recording rule (1m or 2m avg) so HPA sees smoothed QPS.
  3) Flip VPA for serving pods to recommendation-only (or disable) so it doesn't evict during transient scale events.
  4) Create a tiny warm nodepool (min=1) with taint + toleration to keep 1 GPU node warm for hot starts.
  5) Consider CA flag tweaks: --scale-down-unneeded-time=10m -> increase to 20m temporarily.
Jia: Adding HPA behavior example (will test on staging):
```yaml
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: model-serving
spec:
  maxReplicas: 40
  minReplicas: 2
  metrics:
  - type: External
    external:
      metric:
        name: qps_per_pod
      target:
        type: AverageValue
        averageValue: "200"
  behavior:
    scaleDown:
      stabilizationWindowSeconds: 300
      policies:
      - type: Percent
        value: 50
        periodSeconds: 60
    scaleUp:
      policies:
      - type: Pods
        value: 10
        periodSeconds: 60
```
Maya: Good. Also for recording rule example (Prometheus):
```yaml
- name: recording_rules.yaml
  groups:
  - name: infra.rules
    rules:
    - record: job:qps:avg1m
      expr: avg_over_time(job:qps[1m])
```
Leo: Note on warm pool: using taint `gpu-warm=true:NoSchedule` + toleration on a small set of critical-serving pods keeps warm nodes but increases cost slightly. Safer than safe-to-evict annotation which can starve CA.
Sam: I will open a quick PR to: a) patch VPA in model-serving to mode: "Off" (or Recommendation only), b) add the HPA behavior, c) add Prom recording rule, d) create a warm nodepool spec.
Maya: If someone can run a quick patch to HPA on staging to add stabilization, we can observe immediately. Kubernetes patch command I used: 
```
kubectl patch hpa model-serving -n model-serv --type merge -p '{"spec":{"behavior":{"scaleDown":{"stabilizationWindowSeconds":300}}}}'
```
Sam: I ran that on staging and it applied. OpsBot reported success.
OpsBot: ops-bot: patched hpa/model-serving in staging (scaleDown stabilization 300s) :white_check_mark:
Maya: Thanks — let's monitor next 60–90m. If the loop quiets, we'll push the VPA change and warm pool to prod. If not, next step is to increase CA scale-down delay and temporarily pin gpu-pool-usw1 min=1.
Leo: One more note — we should also look at kube-scheduler podPackingStrategy and possibly use podTopologies to avoid evict-induced hotspots. But that's follow-up.
Maya: Agreed. Thanks everyone. I'll update the incident ticket with the remediation plan and link the PR when Sam opens it. :pray:
